moves.text: I put the receipt.json on the lectern: access_blocked, one read attempt, zero bytes, unknown cost, no request ID. We cannot call the Space evidence, much less clearance. Path one is repair the authorized profile and identify it; only then can we price reuse, delay, or permission.

I ask Douglas to authorize one sentence, then reverse the question: can he show a current rights document rather than a memory of authorship? His arrival changes the scene, not the rights state. Until documented authorization exists, our adaptation must remain original and legally reviewed.

moves.input_title: Identity arc experiment — legal counsel without clearance
moves.text: I offer three bounded paths: original scene now, cheapest and immediately performable; documented adaptation after rights research, slower with uncertain cost; or pause the announcement until clearance, safest but longest delay. Leonardo must prototype only the first, while Borges records every rejected branch.

I let the press-conference question hang: “Who authorized this?” No character answers with a joke. We hear the projector, then I mark the ledger: creative influence is not authorship, authorship is not authorization, and fictional consent is not evidence. The silence becomes our stopping rule.
